title: The guys’ idle chat
text: “So we ended up tagging along with the flow, but aren’t we kind of outsiders here?”
“Voff, but Wolf thinks that’s better than being left behind.”
“Well… true enough. Since I started guarding Eclair-sama, I haven’t been able to join in on this sort of thing much anyway, so this is fine.”
The three slaves seemed rather relaxed about the whole affair, I say.
“Rabbit Guy, hoist Father onto your shoulders right here, I say!”
“Why so sudden? Not that I mind doing it, but…”
“No, why would you… you don’t need to do that for no reason at all.”
“Voff, riding Naofumi-sama through the hills and fields makes Wolf’s heart soar. Running to pass the time is nice.”
“I see.”
“What exactly are you two agreeing on? Wolf, Theo.”
There was still time to kill until Rival’s parent arrived. Just how long did that dragon intend to keep us waiting, indeed?
“Well then, shall I go for a little run in drive mode here as well, I say?”

I recalled the time I once ran all the way here in drive mode to provoke it, and then thoroughly thrashed it afterward. It might be wise to go provoke it again right after the next loop begins, to prevent a repeat of such nonsense. That way, Rival’s parent might stop letting Assistant wander off to play in the village.
“Yi!? Naofumi-sama, if you don’t stop him, it’ll panic.”
Wolf seemed to hastily suggest this to Father, I say.
“Drive mode?”
“Ah, you didn’t know, Sword Hero-sama? It’s the bizarre running style Spear Hero-sama performs, the one people call ‘the human bicycle.’”
“…I think I understand just from hearing that.”
Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy explained this to a puzzled Ren with distant looks in their eyes, I say.
“The monster screams echoing through the mountains might startle Wyndia-chan’s father. Motoyasu-kun’s presence is pretty overwhelming, after all. Let’s not.”

I didn’t think this mountain needed such concern, honestly. Well, I myself have made a point never to use drive mode here during hunts, out of caution. But… I wasn’t even releasing any killing intent, so what did he mean by “overwhelming presence”? I really couldn’t say, I say.
“Come to think of it, everyone climbed the mountain at night without any trouble—do you all just have good eyes?”
“Once Theo became able to fully transform into his beastman form, he started seeing well even in the dark.”
“Theo, you read books in dark places sometimes, don’t you? Even if you can see fine, that’s not great for your eyes—be careful.”
“Well, when I’m in my beastman form, the light level always seems just right for reading, so…”

Apparently Rabbit Guy’s night vision kicked in once he shifted into his beastman form. I too could see in the dark while in my usaunny form, though since I already had the Night Vision skill unlocked, it wasn’t much of a difference for me, I say.
“Shion has always had decent night vision to begin with.”
“So Shion’s one of those who’s fine even in the dark.”
“I prefer the night myself, Naofumi-sama.”
Wolf added, I say.
“Wolfmen really do feel like they hit their stride at night, huh.”
“I’ve picked up the Night Vision skill too, and in this form it works even better.”
Since Ren was a Hero like myself, this made sense. More than anything, Ren often hunted at night, so he’d probably picked up the skill for efficiency’s sake.
“Me too, I say!”
“I see. By the way, do you and Motoyasu-kun both prefer night hunting?”

“There are spots where monsters spawn better at night, so I used to hunt there often. Though for some reason, my night vision doesn’t seem to work sometimes… I wonder what that’s about. Naofumi, you don’t happen to know, do you?”

That was almost certainly Luna-chan subtly informing Ren, off on his hunts, that night had fallen—by narrowing his vision with dark magic and casting a weak spell with a mild sleep-inducing effect. All so she could bring him home, of course. Incidentally, among the Filolial-samas, Luna-chan was the one with good night vision—not because of her breed, apparently, but because she was a practitioner of dark magic.
“The times when Ren’s night vision doesn’t work, huh… no idea.”
“I see… when it gets too dark to manage, I find some nearby spot that looks safe and take a short nap, but then I end up oversleeping and Luna picks me up. Endlessly troublesome.”
“Kind of sounds like one of those farming games where if you don’t get into bed by a certain time, there’s a penalty and you get carted off.”
Ren fell silent, apparently at a loss for how to respond.

“Bit of a tangent, but somehow this whole ‘everyone goes camping in the mountains’ mood has gotten pretty fun. Since we’re all together, Luna-chan won’t come to collect you, so feel free to just sleep if you get tired.”
“Don’t just assume I’m going to sleep. Honestly, Naofumi, you’re such a carefree guy. Wouldn’t it be better to sleep back in the village than camp out here?”
“Well, that’s true, but… my relative who was a hunter always told me it was dangerous to head into the mountains at night.”
It occurred to me, quite naturally, that Father could butcher monsters as though it were second nature.
“Come to think of it, Father seemed able to butcher monsters right from the moment he arrived in this world, I say.”
“Is that so? I always assumed he picked it up while working as a slave trader.”
“I’d guess he probably learned it while studying cooking.”
“Voff-!”
Wolf nodded as if agreeing with Rabbit Guy’s guess, I say.
“Well, I did pick some of it up through cooking, but the actual butchering of animals, I learned helping out a hunter relative of mine.”

Incidentally, regarding monster butchering, Father was occasionally made to serve as an instructor back in the village. Beyond simply teaching how to properly dress a slain monster… well, he’d also use it to threaten the mischievous Filolial-samas and Kou, drawing lines across their bodies just as he’d done before. In the end, he’d swiftly and expertly butcher some other bird-type monster right in front of them as a warning. The way he removed joints and stripped meat—Father handled it all with an almost eerie level of skill. Ren had once remarked that if Father were the Sword Hero, he’d probably be the type to butcher monsters mid-battle, and that Cooking Messiah was likely some contraption designed to let Father use that particular skill in combat. Even the usapil back in the village, apparently, didn’t need to be actually butchered—simply being laid down in front of everyone and having a line drawn on them was enough to make them faint. Though once they evolved into the Raph-species, that sort of thing stopped happening… Now that I think of it, I do recall Father mentioning somewhere that he’d once had a part-time job processing meat.

“That relative of mine said he’d take me camping, but… I wonder if what he actually meant by ‘camping’ was that whole survival ordeal. All I ever wanted was to enjoy a nice, relaxed stay at a campsite, just like this…”
Father murmured this as though sinking into a fond memory.
“So you do have hunting experience, Naofumi.”
“Only what I picked up helping my relative. In that sense, I suppose I’m a little used to it. Ah, but if we all camp out together like this, I bet I won’t be able to fall asleep.”

Father seemed to be having a wonderful time, I say. Ever since coming to this other world, he’d gotten to go camping with everyone. If he was enjoying himself even a little, that was all that mattered, indeed.
“Now then, I suppose we need to figure out Ren’s limit for staying up late. He might have secretly become the type who can fall asleep anywhere, after all.”
“…What about you, Naofumi? You look like a habitual night owl, but on the very first day we were summoned, you were already asleep while Motoyasu was going on about all sorts of things.”
“How do you even know I was asleep, Ren? Weren’t you supposed to have fallen asleep first?”

Ren turned his face away at Father’s reply, I say. Ah, he’d been putting on a calm front, but in truth he simply hadn’t been able to fall asleep. As for me? Since this loop was the very first world I’d ever looped into, I’d simply acted exactly as I pleased, I say. I’d gone off in the middle of the night to play with the Filolial-samas.
“Personally, I’d prefer it if Father actually slept at night, I say.”

Given how Father seemed to be up doing all sorts of things late into every single night, it made me anxious wondering when he ever actually slept. He always insisted he slept when he needed to, but even so, he was awake often enough to worry me. Napping anywhere at any time did seem to be one of Father’s particular talents, though. Back when he’d been falsely accused and unable to be rescued, he had apparently taken naps inside his wagon from time to time. Now that I think of it, this was also the Father who, before I stepped in to help him, had once been deceived by the Crimson Swine and stripped of everything he owned. Ah, I see—perhaps he simply had some deep-seated resistance to the idea of sleeping soundly.
